latestPosts.caption:
For years, I trained in a gym where everyone kept to themselves.

Headphones in. Head down. Same weights every session.

I wasn’t lazy. I turned up. I did the sets and reps. But the numbers weren’t moving.

Then I changed gyms. Same me. Same lifts. Different people.

Someone yelling for the last rep. Someone watching your depth. Someone a bit stronger on the next rack.

18 months later, I squatted 200kg. A 40kg PB!

Football teams work the same way.

If the seniors skip breakfast, the juniors skip breakfast. If halftime is water and a laugh, that’s halftime. If recovery is beers and chips, the whole team turns up sore to training.

You can hand a player the perfect plan. If the dressing room laughs at it, it’s dead by Saturday.

Fix the culture and the plan takes care of itself.

Coach, captain, senior player, or the parent on the oranges roster, you’re setting it, whether you mean to or not.

Send this to the one person in your team who needs to see it

latestPosts.caption:
This is what Ashley Young ate the day BEFORE a game 🍝

A massive bowl of carbs. Very little protein. Very little fat.

That’s not by accident.

The carbs you eat the day before get stored in your muscles overnight. That’s the tank your whole game runs on: the sprints, the pressing, and the last 20 minutes.

Most players I work with get this backwards. A normal day before, then they try to cram it all into one big pre-game meal. Then the stomach turns, and the legs still go late.

The tank gets filled the day before. Game day is just a top-up.

If your legs are gone in the second half, this is usually where I start looking.

DM me ANALYSIS and I’ll show you what’s missing in your week 👇

latestPosts.caption:
Matchday on a plate: @adelaideunited goalkeeper @ilona.melegh08 ‘s game day, start to finish 🧤

6:30pm kick-off. Here’s how she fuels it:

8am: Greek yoghurt, muesli, fruit + honey toast
 11am: Banana bread + a big glass of milk
 2pm: Chicken + rice (4.5 hours out, so it’s settled by kick-off)
 4:30pm: Fruit toast + honey, with a small Greek yoghurt
 Warm-up + game: 2 sports drinks, sipped to the final whistle and alternated with water

Full time is where most players drop the ball.

First up, within the hour: a protein shake + a banana. Protein to start the repair, carbs to refuel, and fluid to rehydrate. Easy to get down when you don’t feel like eating.

Then, once her hunger comes back: a burger, and frozen yoghurt with fruit. That’s the payoff. After a battle in goals and a solid week of training like an athlete, she’s earned it. And it still does a job: carbs, protein and colour.

Fuel the week. Enjoy the reward.

💾 Save this for your next game

latestPosts.caption:
Can’t eat before a morning game? You’re not alone.

It’s one of the most common things players tell me. Nerves, early kick-off, stomach feels off, so they skip it and head out on an empty tank.

Then the second half comes and the legs aren’t there.
You don’t need a big meal. You need the right one, at the right time:

🍯 2 to 3 hours out: something light and easy. Toast and honey, a banana, a juice. ⏱️ Not hungry at all? Start small. Even a juice and half a banana is better than nothing. 🍝 Do the heavy lifting the night before. A big carb-based dinner means game day is just a top-up.

Same player. Same game. Different tank.

If your stomach or your energy lets you down on game day, DM me ANALYSIS and I’ll show you what to change 👇

latestPosts.caption:
Same player. Different fuel ⚽

@divanofernandeziglesias is a young player playing for @willemii in Holland who already has first team minutes. But cramps and heavy legs kept showing up late in games.

His match day wasn’t bad. Oats, rice, chicken. The first thing I saw was the gap: hours with almost nothing before kick off, then half a banana. The other half at half time.

Like leaving home with your phone on 20%. It works fine for a while, then dies when you need it most. For Divano, that was the last 20 minutes.

So we started with two quick fixes: 
1️⃣ A proper carb top up 60–90 minutes before kick off 
2️⃣ A real refuel at half time

Next game vs PSV U19: 90 minutes, 2 goals, no issues.
 “I felt good. Still energy in the tank.” – Divano

But the gap was just the first fix. The bigger piece is how much fuel his body needs across the whole week: training days, the day before and match day. That’s what my Football Fuel Analysis works out.

Cramps, heavy legs or low energy late in games? DM me ANALYSIS and I’ll find the one or two things to change first.

Every player is different. Results vary

latestPosts.caption:
Most players I look at aren’t eating badly.

They’re eating too little, at the wrong times.

A small lunch. Nothing before training. A big dinner at 9pm. Then the legs go in the last 20 minutes and they think it’s fitness.

You can’t see it from the inside. That’s what the Football Fuel Analysis is for.

You talk me through one normal training day and a few game-day questions. 30 minutes, nothing to fill in.

I go through it myself. Not an app. Not a template.

You get your Fuel Report within 5 days: what’s already working, the 3 changes that matter most, and your game-day plan hour by hour.

Then we go through it together on a 20-minute call.

If I don’t find at least 3 clear changes, you get a full refund.

I only take 5 players a week so every one gets done properly.

DM me ANALYSIS and I’ll send you the details 👇

What you eat all day decides how you finish the session.

And what you have after decides how you turn up to the next one.

latestPosts.caption:
It started a couple of weeks ago.

“Can I have a hug before I go to sleep?”

Not a quick one. He waits for me to come back in.

That’s when it all comes out. The argument at school. Whose ball it was at lunch. The times tables he’s not sure about. The mate he had the best day with.

Phone stays in the kitchen. I just listen.

He sleeps better. Honestly, so do I.

My job is helping parents fuel their footballers: lunchboxes, training nights, game days, so they’ve got the energy to play their best and grow well. When that part’s sorted, there’s more left at the end of the day for this.

latestPosts.caption:
Training at 5:30. Home at 7. Dinner at 7:45.

That’s 4 hours with nothing in the tank, and they’ve done 60 - 90 minutes of training during that too.

Here’s what a Wednesday actually looks like for an 11 year old training 4 nights a week:

7:15 – Porridge, banana, honey 10:30 – Pretzels, mandarin, cheese stick 12:45 – Chicken wrap + yoghurt 3:30 – Bagel + jam, cucumber, milk 4:45 – Fruit pouch in the car 7:05 – Thermos butter chicken + rice, eaten in the car on the way home

The thermos is the bit most families skip. Dinner doesn’t have to wait until you’re home. It can come with you.

Nothing fancy. Nothing they won’t eat. Just timed around when they actually train.

That’s one day. My meal plans have the other 6, plus the shopping list.

Comment PLAN and I’ll send it through.

latestPosts.caption:
“Can we just keep it on repeat?”

That’s what Jackie sent me a week into the meal plan.

Her son is 14. Plays NPL. Trains 3 nights plus school sessions.

Breakfast was a fight. Two Weet-Bix and he was done. The banana never got touched.

Nothing fancy changed.

Every meal got planned around when he trains. Smaller breakfast. A snack mid-morning to catch up. Proper fuel before the session, not a muesli bar in the car.

Think of it like a road trip. You don’t fill the tank at the last servo before the finish line. You top it up along the way.

A week later, he was trying salmon. And asking for it again.

When a teenager owns the plan, he eats the plan.

The meal plans come in 2, 3 or 4 trainings a week. Pick the one that matches your child’s week.

Comment PLAN and I’ll send you the link.
